### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.extra, mini.pick

### Neovim version

0.13 (!at least latest Nightly build!)

### Description

`MiniExtra.pickers.manpages` builds the env for its `man -k .` command by hand and passes it as `spawn_opts.env`:

https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/ba4362b1728c60f4002e924ebddbb25e21d1b2cf/lua/mini/extra.lua#L1281-L1285

https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/ba4362b1728c60f4002e924ebddbb25e21d1b2cf/lua/mini/extra.lua#L1288

but `HOME` isn't listed, thus stuff like `~/.manpath` isn't included. on NixOS with home-manager, for instance, `home-configuration.nix` can't be found by the picker, whereas `:Man` and `$ man -k .` can still find it.

expected: the picker sees everything `man -k .` sees in a normal shell. adding `HOME` to the env list seems to fix this:

```lua
table.insert(env, vim.env.HOME ~= nil and ('HOME=' .. vim.env.HOME) or nil)
```


### Reproduction

1. Create separate 'nvim-repro' config directory:
    - '~/.config/nvim-repro/' on Unix
    - '~/AppData/Local/nvim-repro/' on Windows

2. Inside 'nvim-repro' directory create a file named 'init.lua'.
   Populate it with the following content:

    ```lua
    -- Clone latest 'mini.nvim' (requires Git CLI installed)
    vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
    local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath('data') .. '/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim'
    local clone_cmd = { 'git', 'clone', '--depth=1', 'https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim', mini_path }
    vim.fn.system(clone_cmd)
    vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw')

    -- Make sure 'mini.nvim' is available
    vim.cmd('packadd mini.nvim')
    require('mini.deps').setup()

    -- Add extra setup steps needed to reproduce the behavior
    -- Use `MiniDeps.add('user/repo')` to install another plugin from GitHub
    require('mini.pick').setup()
    require('mini.extra').setup()
    ```

3. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim` (i.e. execute `nvim` with `NVIM_APPNAME` environment variable set to "nvim-repro").
   Wait for all dependencies to install.

4. Run `:Pick manpages`, search `home-configuration.nix`. No results.

   In the same session, `:terminal man -k home-configuration.nix`. Found
   (`home-configuration.nix (5) - Home Manager configuration specification`).

   Any page that `man -k .` shows in a shell but not in the picker works as a marker.

<details><summary>What to do after reporting an issue</summary>

After reporting the issue, it is safe (and even recommended for cleaner possible future bug reports) to remove 'nvim-repro' config from the system:
- Delete config directory ('~/.config/nvim-repro' on Unix).
- Delete data directory ('~/.local/share/nvim-repro' on Unix).
- Delete state directory ('~/.local/state/nvim-repro' on Unix).

</details>

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

> 4\. Run `:Pick manpages`, search `home-configuration.nix`. No results.

I believe that this might fail, but this is not quite the complete steps for anybody to reproduce (since not everybody uses NixOS). Ideally, I'd appreciate extra steps about how to properly set up the `~/.manpages` to test this.

Since adding a `$HOME` environment variable is probably not a bad idea in itself and is concise enough, the solution should be fine.

title: [mini.extra] `pickers.manpages()` spawns `man` without HOME, ignores per-user man-dbs
